title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 83-85). Grothendieck is writing down a general recipe for a presentation by generators and relations of a groupoid or category τ̃ that lies over a base τ (the functor τ̃ → τ, with fibre categories τ̃_s over s ∈ Ob τ). This is the groupoid analogue of P. Hall's presentation of a group extension 1→N→G→Q→1.

Data on the previous page:
- Generators u'_i of the base τ.
- Relations (8) of the base: loops u'_{i_1}…u'_{i_n} = 1, i.e. words M_α in the u'_i.
- Chosen lifts ũ'_i : s̃_i → t̃_i in τ̃. These need not be composable, see (9).
- A family (a_j) of 'fibre arrows' (10).

On this page:
1. Hypothesis on (a_j). For every s, the a_j lying in τ̃_s generate the arrows of τ̃_s. Consequently every object of τ̃ is a source or target of some a_j.
2. Hypothesis on the lifted relations. Consider each relation α and the consecutive pairs {t̃_{i_ν}, s̃_{i_{ν-1}}} in (9). Because the u'_i in (8) are composable in the base, each pair lies over a single object, i.e. in one fibre. Grothendieck assumes the two points lie in the same connected component of that fibre category.
3. Consequence. There are composable fibre words (zigzags) M_{α,ν}((a_j)) : t̃_{i_ν} ⇝ s̃_{i_{ν-1}}. Inserting them between the lifts turns the non-composable chain (9) into a composable path, displayed as (11):
   s̃_{i_n} →(ũ'_{i_n}) t̃_{i_n} ⇝(M_{α,i_n}) s̃_{i_{n-1}} → … ⇝(M_{α,2}) s̃_{i_1} →(ũ'_{i_1}) t̃_{i_1}.
4. Closing the loop (next page). The composite of (11) maps to the identity loop in the base, so it lies in a fibre. It can therefore be closed by a further fibre word M_{α,1} : t̃_{i_1} ⇝ s̃_{i_n}. This gives the lifted relation (12):
   M_{α,1} ũ' M_{α,2} ũ' … = 1.
5. Remaining relations. Fibre relations N'_β((a_j)) = 1 (13) follow. Presumably the conjugation/action relations for the a_j come later. Together with (12) these should present τ̃.

Purpose. Within cote 146 this is presumably the tool for computing presentations of the Teichmüller groupoids level by level along forgetful fibrations (e.g. forgetting a marked point, fibre ≈ fundamental groupoid of a surface). This is the mechanism behind the 'two-level' generation and relations principle of the Esquisse.
errors: Not an error but a gap: lifting base relations and adding fibre relations is not enough to present τ̃. One also needs relations describing how the lifts ũ'_i act on (conjugate) the fibre generators a_j. On p.85 Grothendieck labels (12) 'commutation' and begins further hypotheses (arrows a_j with target at s̃), so these relations are presumably still to come.

If the fibres are categories rather than groupoids, the connecting 'words' M_{α,ν} must be zigzags; the wavy-arrow notation suggests he means this. The argument implicitly needs τ̃ → τ to behave like a fibration, or at least to have connected fibres along the relevant points.
Order of composition: (8) is written u'_{i_1}…u'_{i_n} with composition right to left, so the path starts at s̃_{i_n}. The diagram is consistent with this.

ideas.what: Presentation of a groupoid fibred over another: generators = fibre generators plus lifts of base generators; relations = fibre relations, lifted base relations closed by fibre words, and conjugation relations.
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of extensions (P. Hall); groupoid version / presentations of fibrations of groupoids
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Hall (groups); groupoid versions in Higgins, R. Brown (Topology and Groupoids) and elsewhere
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Esquisse d'un programme discussion of generators and relations of the Teichmüller tower; not written out there

ideas.what: Condition that consecutive endpoints of lifted generators lie in the same connected component of the fibre, so that lifted base relations can be closed by fibre words.
ideas.modern_name: Connectedness of fibres / lifting of relations in an exact sequence of groupoids

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but standard groupoid generalisation of the presentation of a group extension, written as a lemma for the Teichmüller-tower computations. It is mathematically routine; its interest is only as working material for the two-level principle.
transcription_corrections: 'supposons que ∀α' : the symbol is a struck 'p' followed by α, likely 'pour tout α'.
'dans [...] {+voisins+} des' likely reads 'dans les paires de sommets voisins' (struck variants: 'points', 'sommets').

'{+suppl.+} composabilité' is probably 'qui (par composabilité de la suite des u'_i figurant dans (8)) sont contenus chacun dans une catégorie fibre de τ̃ sur τ'. The second 'composante' is better read as 'sommets': 'les deux sommets soient contenus dans une même composante connexe de la catégorie fibre correspondante'.
'L'hyp. sur (8)' should probably read 'L'hyp. sur (a_j)'. The following line reads roughly 'il existe dans τ̃ un mot composable en les ã_j qui joignent t̃_{i_n} à s̃_{i_{n-1}}, etc.'
In diagram (1) the first arrow is the lift ũ'_{i_n} (tilde over u), and the endpoints carry tildes throughout.
